subject: thick atmosphere
title: What If Earth's Air Were Ten Times Thicker?

scenes.text: What if Earth's air were ten times thicker? The squeeze wouldn't get you. The air itself would.
Ten times the air means the pressure divers feel about 90 meters deep, every second of your life.
Divers start to feel nitrogen narcosis, like being drunk, from about 30 meters. At 90, it's usually incapacitating.
Oxygen turns dangerous too. Above about 1.4 atmospheres of it, seizures can strike. You'd be breathing 2.1.
Even breathing gets harder. Air ten times denser takes much more effort to pull through your airways.
Deep divers survive this by swapping nitrogen for helium. Venus shows the extreme: about 92 times our air, like a kilometer underwater.

description:
What if Earth's air were ten times thicker? Ten atmospheres is the pressure about 90 meters underwater, where breathing ordinary air brings incapacitating nitrogen narcosis and oxygen above the 1.4-atmosphere toxicity threshold.
Venus's surface pressure is about 92 bar.
